1	// Program Buffer execution helpers for the RISC-V Debug Module.
2	//
3	// Follows the same duck-typed template pattern as dmi_poll.hpp so that
4	// resume_driver.hpp can include this header without a circular dependency.
5	// Bus type requirement: write(uint8_t reg, uint32_t val) and
6	//                       read(uint8_t reg) -> uint32_t.
7	//
8	// Debug Spec references: section 3.6 (Program Buffer), table 3.1 (DMI),
9	// section 3.7.1.3 (Abstract Command - Access Register).
10	
11	#pragma once
12	
13	#include "hybrid/abstract_command.hpp"
14	#include "hybrid/dmi_poll.hpp"
15	
16	#include <array>
17	#include <cstdint>
18	#include <cstdio>
19	#include <span>
20	#include <stdexcept>
21	#include <string>
22	
23	namespace hybrid {
24	
25	// DMI address of the first Program Buffer register (progbuf0..progbuf15).
26	inline constexpr uint8_t kProgbuf0 = 0x20u;
27	
28	// Max payload instructions: 16 total slots minus 1 reserved for the
29	// mandatory ebreak that terminates execution.
30	inline constexpr std::size_t kProgbufMaxInsns = 15u;
31	
32	// Standard ebreak encoding (funct12=1, opcode=SYSTEM).
33	inline constexpr uint32_t kEbreak = 0x00100073u;
34	
35	// "Execute Program Buffer only" command (Debug Spec table 3.1):
36	//   cmdtype  = 0 (Access Register)
37	//   aarsize  = Bits64 (3) - ignored by DM when transfer=0, set for consistency
38	//   postexec = 1 (bit 18)
39	//   transfer = 0 (bit 17 NOT set) - skip register I/O, only run progbuf
40	//   write    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
41	//   regno    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
42	inline constexpr uint32_t kExecProgbufCmd =
43	    (uint32_t(AarSize::Bits64) & 0x7u) << 20 | (1u << 18);
44	
45	// Encode `vsetvl rd, rs1, rs2` (RVV 1.0 section 6.2, funct7=1000000).
46	// Tier-B restore: stage vl in rs1 and vtype in rs2 via Abstract Commands,
47	// then branch-free-restore both in one Program Buffer execution.
48	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vsetvl(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, uint8_t rs2)
49	{
50	    return (0b1000000u << 25)
51	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
52	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
53	         | (0b111u << 12)
54	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
55	         | 0x57u;  // OP-V opcode
56	}
57	
58	// Encode `csrrw rd, csr, rs1` (SYSTEM opcode, funct3=001).
59	// Tier-A PB fallback: stage the CSR value in rs1 via Abstract Command,
60	// then write it to a CSR that the DM cannot reach via abstract access.
61	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_csrrw(uint8_t rd, uint16_t csr, uint8_t rs1)
62	{
63	    return ((uint32_t(csr) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
64	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
65	         | (0b001u << 12)
66	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
67	         | 0x73u;  // SYSTEM opcode
68	}
69	
70	// Encode `csrrs rd, csr, rs1` (SYSTEM opcode, funct3=010). With rs1=x0 this is
71	// `csrr rd, csr`: a pure CSR read (the RISC-V spec suppresses the write side
72	// effect when rs1=x0). The CSR drain sweep reads each supported Andes/M-ext CSR
73	// into a temp GPR with this, then sd's it to the scratch page.
74	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_csrrs(uint8_t rd, uint16_t csr, uint8_t rs1)
75	{
76	    return ((uint32_t(csr) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
77	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
78	         | (0b010u << 12)
79	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
80	         | 0x73u;  // SYSTEM opcode
81	}
82	
83	// Encode `vle8.v vd, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector load, EEW=8 (RVV 1.0 sec 7.4).
84	// Fields: vm=1 (unmasked, bit 25), width=000, mop=00, mew=0, nf=000,
85	// lumop=00000, opcode LOAD-FP=0x07. PB V-regfile reload sweeps v0..v31 from
86	// the shared scratch region after a vsetvl to e8/m1.
87	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vle8_v(uint8_t vd, uint8_t rs1)
88	{
89	    return (1u << 25)
90	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
91	         | ((uint32_t(vd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
92	         | 0x07u;  // LOAD-FP opcode
93	}
94	
95	// Encode `vse8.v vs3, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector store, EEW=8. Mirror of
96	// encode_vle8_v with opcode STORE-FP=0x27. PB V-regfile dump sweeps v0..v31
97	// back to the shared scratch region at drain.
98	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vse8_v(uint8_t vs3, uint8_t rs1)
99	{
100	    return (1u << 25)
101	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
102	         | ((uint32_t(vs3) & 0x1Fu) << 7)
103	         | 0x27u;  // STORE-FP opcode
104	}
105	
106	// Encode `addi rd, rs1, imm12` (OP-IMM opcode 0x13, funct3=000). The batched
107	// V-data sweep advances the scratch base pointer x7 by one register-span
108	// between transfers WITHIN a Program-Buffer execution, so the per-register
109	// abstract x7 write disappears. imm12 is a signed 12-bit field (-2048..2047).
110	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_addi(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
111	{
112	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
113	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
114	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
115	         | 0x13u;  // OP-IMM opcode (funct3=000)
116	}
117	
118	// Encode `ld rd, imm12(rs1)` (LOAD opcode 0x03, funct3=011 for 64-bit). The GPR
119	// block-load sweeps x1..x31 from a scratch region addressed by a base register,
120	// so 31 abstract register writes collapse into a few Program-Buffer executions.
121	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_ld(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
122	{
123	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
124	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
125	         | (0b011u << 12)
126	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
127	         | 0x03u;  // LOAD opcode
128	}
129	
130	// Encode `fld rd, imm12(rs1)` (LOAD-FP opcode 0x07, funct3=011 for double). Same
131	// shape as encode_ld with the FP-load opcode: the FPR block-load sweeps f0..f31
132	// from the scratch region via an integer base register, collapsing 32 abstract
133	// FPR writes into a few Program-Buffer executions.
134	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_fld(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
135	{
136	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
137	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
138	         | (0b011u << 12)
139	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
140	         | 0x07u;  // LOAD-FP opcode
141	}
142	
143	// Encode `sd rs2, imm12(rs1)` (STORE opcode 0x23, funct3=011 for 64-bit). The
144	// mirror of encode_ld for the DRAIN direction: the GPR drain sweeps x1..x30 from
145	// the regfile INTO the scratch region via an integer base register, collapsing
146	// 31 abstract reads into a few Program-Buffer executions. S-type splits the
147	// signed 12-bit immediate: imm[11:5] -> bits 31:25, imm[4:0] -> bits 11:7.
148	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_sd(uint8_t rs2, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
149	{
150	    const uint32_t imm = uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu;
151	    return ((imm >> 5) & 0x7Fu) << 25
152	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
153	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
154	         | (0b011u << 12)
155	         | ((imm & 0x1Fu) << 7)
156	         | 0x23u;  // STORE opcode
157	}
158	
159	// Encode `fsd rs2, imm12(rs1)` (STORE-FP opcode 0x27, funct3=011 for double).
160	// Same S-type shape as encode_sd with the FP-store opcode: the FPR drain sweeps
161	// f0..f31 from the regfile into the scratch region via an integer base register.
162	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_fsd(uint8_t rs2, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
163	{
164	    const uint32_t imm = uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu;
165	    return ((imm >> 5) & 0x7Fu) << 25
166	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
167	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
168	         | (0b011u << 12)
169	         | ((imm & 0x1Fu) << 7)
170	         | 0x27u;  // STORE-FP opcode
171	}
172	
173	// Write insns[0..n-1] to progbuf0..n-1 and kEbreak to progbuf[n].
174	// Clears any sticky abstractcs.cmderr (W1C), issues kExecProgbufCmd, polls
175	// until abstractcs.busy clears, then verifies cmderr stayed clear.
176	//
177	// Throws std::runtime_error if insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns, if the poll
178	// times out, or if the DM raises cmderr during execution. No caller has a
179	// legitimate reason to silently continue on PB failure - the hart state
180	// would be partially restored / partially drained, which is worse than
181	// surfacing the fault.
182	template<typename Bus>
183	inline void exec_progbuf(Bus& bus, std::span<const uint32_t> insns)
184	{
185	    if (insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns)
186	        throw std::runtime_error(
187	            "exec_progbuf: too many instructions ("
188	            + std::to_string(insns.size()) + " > "
189	            + std::to_string(kProgbufMaxInsns) + ")");
190	
191	    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < insns.size(); ++i)
192	        bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + i), insns[i]);
193	    bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + insns.size()), kEbreak);
194	
195	    if ((bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask) != 0u)
196	        bus.write(kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsCmderrMask);
197	
198	    bus.write(kDmiCommand, kExecProgbufCmd);
199	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy, "exec_progbuf busy");
200	
201	    const uint32_t cmderr = bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask;
202	    if (cmderr != 0u)
203	        throw std::runtime_error(
204	            "exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr="
205	            + std::to_string(cmderr >> 8));
206	}
207	
208	// vtype encoding for e8, m8, ta, ma (vsew=000, vlmul=011, vta=1, vma=1). The
209	// V-data sweep uses LMUL=8 so one vle8.v/vse8.v moves a whole group of 8
210	// registers (8*vlenb byte-elements, vl=8*vlenb) in a single instruction.
211	inline constexpr uint32_t kVtypeE8M8 = 0xC3u;
212	
213	// Abstract-command write of a 64-bit value to Debug Module register `regno`
214	// (GPR/CSR/FPR): DATA0/DATA1 + Access-Register(write) + busy-poll. Free
215	// function so ResumeDriver, StateDrain, and the V-data sweep share one copy.
216	template<typename Bus>
217	inline void write_register_abstract(Bus& bus, uint16_t regno, uint64_t value)
218	{
219	    bus.write(kDmiData0, static_cast<uint32_t>(value & 0xffffffffu));
220	    bus.write(kDmiData1, static_cast<uint32_t>((value >> 32) & 0xffffffffu));
221	    bus.write(kDmiCommand,
222	              access_register_command(regno, AarSize::Bits64, /*write=*/true));
223	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy,
224	                     "write_register_abstract");
225	}
226	
227	// Program-Buffer block sweep: seed integer base register `base_gpr` with
228	// `base_gpa`, then run `encode(reg, base_gpr, (reg-first_reg)*8)` for reg in
229	// [first_reg, last_reg) through the Program Buffer, batched at (progbufsize-1)
230	// instructions per execution (one slot reserved for the terminating ebreak).
231	// One uniform load/store encoder drives it, so the GPR/FPR restore (ld/fld,
232	// scratch -> regfile) and the GPR/FPR drain (sd/fsd, regfile -> scratch) share
233	// one implementation: ~32 registers move in ~6 halted-hart round-trips instead
234	// of ~32 abstract commands, and the values ride the shared scratch page, not
235	// DMI. The 8-byte-strided offset spans every slot (<= 248, within ld/sd's
236	// signed 12-bit immediate). The caller guarantees base_gpr is safe to seed: on
237	// a load it may be a swept register that rides LAST (its own load runs after
238	// every other use of it as the base); on a store it must be EXCLUDED from
239	// [first_reg, last_reg) -- seeding destroys its value before it could be stored
240	// -- and captured separately.
241	template<typename Bus>
242	inline void pb_block_sweep(Bus& bus, uint8_t base_gpr, uint64_t base_gpa,
243	                           uint8_t first_reg, uint8_t last_reg,
244	                           uint32_t (*encode)(uint8_t, uint8_t, int32_t))
245	{
246	    // The Program Buffer holds abstractcs.progbufsize entries (this DM reports
247	    // 8); reserve one slot for the terminating ebreak, so at most progbufsize-1
248	    // load/store insns per execution.
249	    const uint32_t progbufsize = (bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) >> 24) & 0x1Fu;
250	    const std::size_t max_ops = (progbufsize > 1) ? progbufsize - 1u : 1u;
251	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(base_gpr), base_gpa);  // base pointer
252	    std::array<uint32_t, 32> batch{};
253	    std::size_t n = 0;
254	    for (uint8_t k = first_reg; k < last_reg; ++k) {
255	        batch[n++] = encode(k, base_gpr,
256	                            static_cast<int32_t>((k - first_reg) * 8));
257	        if (n == max_ops || k + 1 == last_reg) {
258	            exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{batch.data(), n});
259	            n = 0;
260	        }
261	    }
262	}
263	
264	// Direction for csr_sweep: Restore writes each CSR from the scratch page
265	// (ld + csrrw), Drain reads each CSR back to scratch (csrr + sd).
266	enum class CsrSweepDir { Restore, Drain };
267	
268	// Program-Buffer CSR sweep: transport a caps-supported list of CSRs between the
269	// hart and the scratch page. Unlike pb_block_sweep (one uniform ld/st per
270	// register), a CSR needs TWO instructions -- the CSR number is baked into the
271	// csrrw/csrr immediate, so it cannot be a runtime operand -- so this batches at
272	// (progbufsize-1)/2 CSRs per Program-Buffer execution:
273	//   Restore: ld val,(k*8)(base); csrrw x0, csrs[k], val   (scratch -> CSR)
274	//   Drain:   csrr val, csrs[k];  sd val,(k*8)(base)       (CSR -> scratch)
275	// `base` is an integer GPR seeded once with `base_gpa` (the CSR scratch region);
276	// `val` is a temp GPR the caller may clobber. The values ride the shared scratch
277	// page (staged/lifted by stage_csr_to_scratch / read_csr_from_scratch), not DMI.
278	// The csrs list is the caps-supported set in the SAME canonical order the host
279	// stager packs, so slot k*8 holds csrs[k]'s value. Empty list -> no-op (not even
280	// the base seed). The k*8 offset spans every slot (<= 81*8 = 648 < 2047).
281	//
282	// Every csrs[k] MUST be implemented by the target (the caller builds the list
283	// from caps): a csrrw/csrr to an unimplemented CSR raises cmderr and exec_progbuf
284	// throws, aborting the whole batch. That is intentional -- a faulting sweep means
285	// the caps map is wrong, a config bug to fix, not something to silently mirror.
286	// To make that bug FIXABLE, a faulting batch is re-run one CSR at a time and the
287	// thrown error names the offending CSR (re-running is safe: drain reads are
288	// idempotent, and a restore re-applies the same staged values).
289	template<typename Bus>
290	inline void csr_sweep(Bus& bus, uint8_t base_gpr, uint64_t base_gpa,
291	                      uint8_t val_gpr, std::span<const uint16_t> csrs,
292	                      CsrSweepDir dir)
293	{
294	    if (csrs.empty()) return;
295	    const uint32_t progbufsize = (bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) >> 24) & 0x1Fu;
296	    // Two insns per CSR; reserve one slot for the terminating ebreak. Clamp to
297	    // the ebreak-adjusted payload cap so a batch never overruns the buffer.
298	    std::size_t usable = (progbufsize > 1) ? progbufsize - 1u : 1u;
299	    if (usable > kProgbufMaxInsns) usable = kProgbufMaxInsns;
300	    const std::size_t max_csrs = (usable >= 2) ? usable / 2u : 1u;
301	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(base_gpr), base_gpa);  // scratch base
302	    // The (transport; ld/sd) insn pair for csrs[k], shared by the batch build
303	    // and the fault bisect so both run the identical instructions.
304	    const auto pair_for = [&](std::size_t k) -> std::array<uint32_t, 2> {
305	        const int32_t off = static_cast<int32_t>(k * 8);
306	        if (dir == CsrSweepDir::Restore)
307	            return {encode_ld(val_gpr, base_gpr, off),
308	                    encode_csrrw(0, csrs[k], val_gpr)};
309	        return {encode_csrrs(val_gpr, csrs[k], 0),
310	                encode_sd(val_gpr, base_gpr, off)};
311	    };
312	    std::array<uint32_t, 32> batch{};
313	    std::size_t n = 0, in_batch = 0;
314	    for (std::size_t k = 0; k < csrs.size(); ++k) {
315	        const auto pair = pair_for(k);
316	        batch[n++] = pair[0];
317	        batch[n++] = pair[1];
318	        if (++in_batch == max_csrs || k + 1 == csrs.size()) {
319	            try {
320	                exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{batch.data(), n});
321	            } catch (const std::runtime_error&) {
322	                for (std::size_t j = k + 1 - in_batch; j <= k; ++j) {
323	                    const auto one = pair_for(j);
324	                    try {
325	                        exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{one});
326	                    } catch (const std::runtime_error&) {
327	                        char addr[8];
328	                        std::snprintf(addr, sizeof addr, "0x%x", csrs[j]);
329	                        throw std::runtime_error(
330	                            std::string{"csr_sweep: CSR "} + addr
331	                            + " raised cmderr -- the caps map over-claims a CSR"
332	                              " the hart does not implement (fix andes_caps)");
333	                    }
334	                }
335	                throw;  // no single CSR reproduced the batch fault
336	            }
337	            n = 0;
338	            in_batch = 0;
339	        }
340	    }
341	}

343	// Sweep all 32 V data registers between the hart regfile and the vlenb-packed
344	// scratch region via the Program Buffer. load=true issues vle8.v
345	// (scratch -> regfile, on resume); load=false issues vse8.v (regfile ->
346	// scratch, at drain). The leading vsetvl to e8/m8 sets vl=8*vlenb and forces
347	// vstart=0, so one unit-stride access covers a whole LMUL=8 group of 8
348	// registers. Uses x5/x6 (vsetvl operands) and x7 (group base pointer) as
349	// scratch. `vlenb` is the runtime per-register width; the scratch must be
350	// packed at vlenb stride (stage_v_to_scratch) so each 8-register group is
351	// contiguous.
352	template<typename Bus>
353	inline void pb_v_data_sweep(Bus& bus, uint64_t scratch_gpa, uint64_t vlenb,
354	                            bool load)
355	{
356	    // The scratch holds v0..v31 packed contiguously at vlenb stride (see
357	    // stage_v_to_scratch), so 8 consecutive registers form one LMUL=8 group.
358	    // One vle8.v/vse8.v then moves a whole group (8*vlenb contiguous bytes,
359	    // vl=8*vlenb) and all 32 registers transfer in 4 grouped ops -- whose 4
360	    // (transfer; addi) pairs fit in a SINGLE Program-Buffer execution. Each PB
361	    // execution is one halted-hart DM round-trip (~1000 sim cycles in the
362	    // busy-poll), so this is the floor: one vsetvl + one grouped execution. The
363	    // register bytes never cross DMI; they ride the shared mmap.
364	    constexpr unsigned     kRegsPerGroup   = 8;  // LMUL=8
365	    // kVtypeE8M8's vlmul field (bits 2:0) must encode this LMUL, so one grouped
366	    // vle8.v/vse8.v really covers kRegsPerGroup registers (integer LMUL=1<<vlmul;
367	    // 0xC3 & 7 == 3 -> LMUL 8).
368	    static_assert((1u << (kVtypeE8M8 & 0x7u)) == kRegsPerGroup,
369	                  "kVtypeE8M8 must encode LMUL = kRegsPerGroup");
370	    constexpr std::size_t  kGroupSweepInsns = (32 / kRegsPerGroup) * 2;  // (ld;addi)*4
371	    static_assert(kGroupSweepInsns <= kProgbufMaxInsns,
372	                  "the grouped sweep must fit one Program Buffer execution");
373	    const uint64_t group_bytes = static_cast<uint64_t>(kRegsPerGroup) * vlenb;
374	    if (group_bytes > 2047)  // addi imm12 is signed 12-bit; max 8*128 = 1024
375	        throw std::runtime_error(
376	            "pb_v_data_sweep: 8*vlenb exceeds the addi imm12 range");
377	
378	    // vsetvl to e8/m8 with AVL = 8*vlenb sets vl = VLMAX = 8*vlenb (one
379	    // byte-element per lane across the whole group) and forces vstart = 0.
380	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(5), group_bytes);  // AVL
381	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(6), kVtypeE8M8);   // e8, m8, ta, ma
382	    const std::array<uint32_t, 1> pb_vsetvl = { encode_vsetvl(0, 5, 6) };
383	    exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{pb_vsetvl});
384	
385	    // Base pointer x7 staged once; the in-buffer addi advances it one group at
386	    // a time. The group base register must be LMUL-aligned: v0/v8/v16/v24.
387	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(7), scratch_gpa);
388	    const uint32_t addi_step =
389	        encode_addi(7, 7, static_cast<int32_t>(group_bytes));
390	    std::array<uint32_t, kGroupSweepInsns> group_sweep{};
391	    std::size_t n = 0;
392	    for (uint8_t g = 0; g < 32; g += kRegsPerGroup) {
393	        group_sweep[n++] = load ? encode_vle8_v(g, 7) : encode_vse8_v(g, 7);
394	        group_sweep[n++] = addi_step;  // last group's addi is harmless dead work
395	    }
396	    exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{group_sweep.data(), n});
397	}

1	// Andes-CSR capability gating.
2	//
3	// A core implements an Andes custom CSR only when the matching feature is
4	// configured into it (config.inc). Restoring a CSR the target core lacks can
5	// hang the DMI handshake -- observed on ax45mpv_premium for ucode (no DSP) and
6	// mecc_code (no ECC). So the resume/drain loops transport only the CSRs the
7	// target core supports, decided here from the core's feature gates.
8	//
9	// This header is Verilator/SystemC-free: it maps a CSR address to its gate and
10	// answers "does a core with these gates support this CSR". The binding of each
11	// gate to the core's compiled-in `_NDS_*` config macros lives in the sim binary
12	// (see andes_caps_from_config), so this stays unit-testable in isolation.
13	#ifndef ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
14	#define ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
15	
16	#include <cstdint>
17	#include <string>
18	#include <vector>
19	
20	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"

24	// The hardware feature that gates each transported CSR. ALWAYS = unconditionally
25	// present (a base machine CSR every core has; never gated off). The first block
26	// gates the v3 Andes custom CSRs; the second block (UMODE..TRIGGER) gates the v4
27	// M-ext CSRs (HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST) -- standard + Andes M-mode CSRs whose
28	// existence depends on a privilege level or extension the core may not have.
29	enum class AndesGate : uint8_t {
30	  ALWAYS = 0,
31	  DSP,
32	  CODENSE,
33	  ZCMT,        // standard Zcmt table jump (jvt); NOT implied by CoDense
34	  POWERBRAKE,
35	  STACKSAFE,
36	  ECC,
37	  PMA,
38	  ILM,
39	  DLM,
40	  PERF_MONITOR,
41	  // v4 M-ext gates.
42	  UMODE,       // needs U-mode  (NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
43	  SMODE,       // needs S-mode  (NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS == 3)
44	  EPMP,        // ePMP / Smepmp (mseccfg)
45	  SMRNMI,      // resumable NMI (mnscratch/mnepc/mncause/mnstatus/mnvec/mrnxvec)
46	  EXCSLVL,     // exception save levels (msave*)
47	  CLIC,        // CLIC / enhanced CLIC (mtvt/mintthresh/mcirq_entry)
48	  SMSTATEEN,   // state-enable (mstateen0..3)
49	  CCTL,        // cache control CSRs (mcctlbeginaddr/mcctldata)
50	  PPI,         // private peripheral interface base (mppib)
51	  FIO,         // fast IO base (mfiob)
52	  TRIGGER,     // debug triggers (tselect/tdata1/tdata2/tcontrol/mcontext)
53	};
54	
55	// Map an Andes CSR (by address) to the feature gate that enables it. Addresses
56	// are the HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST scalars plus the PMA block. A CSR with no
57	// custom-extension gate is ALWAYS (a base machine CSR every Andes core has).
58	// Maintainer note: a CSR added to HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST that needs gating must
59	// get a case here, else it defaults to ALWAYS (transported unconditionally).
60	constexpr AndesGate andes_gate_for(uint16_t csr_addr)
61	{
62	  switch (csr_addr) {
63	    case 0x801: return AndesGate::DSP;           // ucode (DSP overflow flag)
64	    case 0x800: return AndesGate::CODENSE;        // uitb  (CoDense table base)
65	    // jvt is Zcmt's table-jump base, NOT part of classic CoDense (exec.it +
66	    // uitb): a CoDense core without Zcmt faults a csrr of it (seen on
67	    // ax45mpv_premium, where it aborted the drain CSR sweep).
68	    case 0x017: return AndesGate::ZCMT;           // jvt   (Zcmt only)
69	    case 0x7C5: return AndesGate::POWERBRAKE;     // mpft_ctl
70	    case 0x7C2: return AndesGate::ECC;            // mecc_code
71	    case 0x7C6:                                   // mhsp_ctl
72	    case 0x7C7:                                   // msp_bound
73	    case 0x7C8: return AndesGate::STACKSAFE;      // msp_base
74	    case 0x7C0: return AndesGate::ILM;            // milmb (ILM base)
75	    case 0x7C1: return AndesGate::DLM;            // mdlmb (DLM base)
76	    // v4 M-ext CSR gates (HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST).
77	    // The counter-mask trio mcountermask_m (0x7D1), mcountermask_u (0x7D3),
78	    // mcounterwen (0x7CE) needs user mode (spec existence: PMNDS & misa[20]);
79	    // an M-only core does not implement them (a PB csrr faults cmderr=3,
80	    // aborting a CSR sweep), so gate them UMODE -- not PERF_MONITOR.
81	    case 0x30A: case 0x306: case 0x7D3:           // menvcfg, mcounteren, mcountermask_u
82	    case 0x7CE: case 0x7D1:                       // mcounterwen, mcountermask_m
83	    case 0x808: case 0x80B: case 0x811: case 0x813:  // uzobctl, ucctlbeginaddr, sleepvalue, umisc_ctl
84	      return AndesGate::UMODE;
85	    case 0x7D2: case 0x7D5: return AndesGate::SMODE;  // mcountermask_s, mslideleg
86	    case 0x747: return AndesGate::EPMP;           // mseccfg
87	    case 0x320: case 0xB03: case 0xB04: case 0xB05: case 0xB06:  // mcountinhibit, mhpmcounter3-6
88	    case 0x323: case 0x324: case 0x325: case 0x326:              // mhpmevent3-6
89	    case 0x7CF:                                                  // mcounterinten (PMNDS only)
90	      return AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR;
91	    case 0x740: case 0x741: case 0x742: case 0x744:  // mnscratch, mnepc, mncause, mnstatus
92	    case 0x7C3: case 0x7DE:                           // mnvec, mrnxvec
93	      return AndesGate::SMRNMI;
94	    case 0x7C9: return AndesGate::ALWAYS;         // mdcause (base Andes trap CSR)
95	    case 0x7D6: case 0x7D7: case 0x7D8: case 0x7D9:  // msavestatus, msaveepc1, msavecause1, msaveepc2
96	    case 0x7DA: case 0x7DB: case 0x7DC:              // msavecause2, msavedcause1, msavedcause2
97	      return AndesGate::EXCSLVL;
98	    case 0x307: case 0x347: case 0x7EC:           // mtvt, mintthresh, mcirq_entry
99	      return AndesGate::CLIC;
100	    case 0x30C: case 0x30D: case 0x30E: case 0x30F:  // mstateen0..3
101	      return AndesGate::SMSTATEEN;
102	    case 0x7CB: case 0x7CD: return AndesGate::CCTL;  // mcctlbeginaddr, mcctldata
103	    case 0x7F0: return AndesGate::PPI;            // mppib
104	    case 0x7F1: return AndesGate::FIO;            // mfiob
105	    case 0x7A0: case 0x7A1: case 0x7A2: case 0x7A5: case 0x7A8:  // tselect, tdata1, tdata2, tcontrol, mcontext
106	      return AndesGate::TRIGGER;
107	    default:
108	      // PMA cfg (0xBC0, 0xBC2) and addr (0xBD0..0xBDF) blocks.
109	      if (csr_addr == HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR || csr_addr == HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR + 2)
110	        return AndesGate::PMA;
111	      if (csr_addr >= HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR &&
112	          csr_addr < HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR + HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM)
113	        return AndesGate::PMA;
114	      return AndesGate::ALWAYS;                    // mxstatus 0x7C4, mclk_ctl 0x7DF
115	  }
116	}

118	// The set of Andes feature gates a target core has on. Built from the core's
119	// compiled-in config (config.inc) in the sim binary and injected into the
120	// resume/drain loops, so they transport only the CSRs the core implements.
121	// Default = every gate on (all(): no gating, the prior unconditional behavior).
122	struct AndesCaps {
123	  uint32_t gate_mask = ~0u;
124	
125	  static constexpr AndesCaps all()  { return AndesCaps{~0u}; }
126	  static constexpr AndesCaps none() { return AndesCaps{0u}; }
127	
128	  constexpr void set(AndesGate g, bool on = true)
129	  {
130	    const uint32_t bit = 1u << static_cast<unsigned>(g);
131	    if (on) gate_mask |= bit;
132	    else    gate_mask &= ~bit;
133	  }
134	
135	  constexpr bool gate_on(AndesGate g) const
136	  {
137	    return (gate_mask >> static_cast<unsigned>(g)) & 1u;
138	  }
139	
140	  // ALWAYS-gated CSRs are present on every core regardless of the mask.
141	  constexpr bool supports_csr(uint16_t csr_addr) const
142	  {
143	    const AndesGate g = andes_gate_for(csr_addr);
144	    return g == AndesGate::ALWAYS || gate_on(g);
145	  }
146	};

148	// The gated CSR names this core supports, for the --describe card. Iterates the
149	// two single-source-of-truth X-macro lists: the v3 Andes custom CSRs and the v4
150	// M-ext CSRs. The driver uses this list to gate --verify, so a CSR the core
151	// lacks is neither restored, drained, nor compared.
152	inline std::vector<std::string> supported_andes_csr_names(const AndesCaps& caps)
153	{
154	  std::vector<std::string> out;
155	#define X(field, addr, name) if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) out.push_back(name);
156	  HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)
157	#undef X
158	  // PMA group markers (whole pmacfg[]/pmaaddr[] blocks share one gate), so a
159	  // consumer can include/exclude PMA without listing all 18 entries.
160	  if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR))  out.push_back("pmacfg");
161	  if (caps.supports_csr(HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR)) out.push_back("pmaaddr");
162	  // v4 M-ext CSRs share the same address->gate map and --describe list.
163	#define X(field, addr, name) if (caps.supports_csr(addr)) out.push_back(name);
164	  HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST(X)
165	#undef X
166	  return out;
167	}

// Build an AndesCaps from the core's compiled-in config.inc feature macros
// (_NDS_*, supplied by the build-generated cpu_config.hpp). This is the ONE
// place that binds each Andes feature gate to its config macro -- the sim-binary
// counterpart of the Verilator-free andes_caps.hpp, kept separate so the unit
// tests never need the generated header.
//
// PRECONDITION: the _NDS_* macros must already be in scope (include this AFTER
// cpu_config.hpp). A macro that is absent reads as "feature off" (gate clear),
// never a compile error -- so a core whose config omits a knob stays safe.
#pragma once

#include "hybrid/andes_caps.hpp"

namespace hybrid {

inline AndesCaps andes_caps_from_config()
{
  AndesCaps c = AndesCaps::none();

#if defined(_NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_DSP_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::DSP);           // ucode
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::CODENSE);       // uitb
#endif
  // Zcmt (jvt): no current config.inc generation carries a Zcmt knob, so the
  // gate stays off (absent reads as "feature off"). Bound here so a future
  // config that grows the macro turns it on without a code change.
#if defined(_NDS_ZCMT_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_ZCMT_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::ZCMT);          // jvt
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::POWERBRAKE);    // mpft_ctl
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT) && _NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::STACKSAFE);     // mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT) && _NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR_INT
  c.set(AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR);  // mcountinhibit, mhpm*, mcounterinten
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_PMA_ENTRIES) && (_NDS_PMA_ENTRIES > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::PMA);           // pmacfg / pmaaddr
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::ILM);           // milmb
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::DLM);           // mdlmb
#endif
  // ECC: mecc_code exists if ANY RAM block is configured with ECC.
#if (defined(_NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) && _NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) || \
    (defined(_NDS_ICACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) && _NDS_ICACHE_ECC_TYPE_INT) || \
    (defined(_NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    && _NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    || \
    (defined(_NDS_DLM_ECC_TYPE_INT)    && _NDS_DLM_ECC_TYPE_INT)
  c.set(AndesGate::ECC);           // mecc_code
#endif

  // v4 M-ext gates. Privilege-level gates from NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS
  // (1 = M, 2 = M+U, 3 = M+S+U). An absent knob reads as off -- safe.
#if defined(_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS) && (_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
  c.set(AndesGate::UMODE);         // menvcfg, mcounteren, mcountermask_u, U-delta
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS) && (_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 3)
  c.set(AndesGate::SMODE);         // mcountermask_s, mslideleg
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_NUM_TRIGGER) && (_NDS_NUM_TRIGGER > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::TRIGGER);       // tselect, tdata1, tdata2, tcontrol, mcontext
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_SMEPMP) && _NDS_SMEPMP) || (defined(_NDS_EPMP) && _NDS_EPMP)
  c.set(AndesGate::EPMP);          // mseccfg
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_SMRNMI) && _NDS_SMRNMI) || (defined(_NDS_RNMI) && _NDS_RNMI)
  c.set(AndesGate::SMRNMI);        // mnscratch/mnepc/mncause/mnstatus/mnvec/mrnxvec
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_EXCSLVL) && (_NDS_EXCSLVL > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::EXCSLVL);       // msave*
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_ECLIC) && _NDS_ECLIC) || (defined(_NDS_CLIC) && _NDS_CLIC)
  c.set(AndesGate::CLIC);          // mtvt, mintthresh, mcirq_entry
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_SMSTATEEN) && _NDS_SMSTATEEN
  c.set(AndesGate::SMSTATEEN);     // mstateen0..3
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_CCTLCSR) && _NDS_CCTLCSR) || (defined(_NDS_CCTL) && _NDS_CCTL)
  c.set(AndesGate::CCTL);          // mcctlbeginaddr, mcctldata
#endif
#if defined(_NDS_PPI_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_PPI_SIZE_KB > 0)
  c.set(AndesGate::PPI);           // mppib
#endif
#if (defined(_NDS_FIO_SIZE_KB) && (_NDS_FIO_SIZE_KB > 0)) || \
    (defined(_NDS_FIO) && _NDS_FIO)
  c.set(AndesGate::FIO);           // mfiob
#endif

  return c;
}

}  // namespace hybrid

    COMMENT "Copying config.inc for ${CPU_NAME}"

  add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT "${_config_object}"

    WORKING_DIRECTORY "${OBJ_SC_DIR}"
    DEPENDS "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/config.inc"
    COMMENT "Building config object for ${CPU_NAME}"
  )

  # riscv-cpu"` matches `-cpu andes-<family>`. No converter -> empty cfg.
  string(REGEX REPLACE "_.*$" "" QEMU_CPU_FAMILY "${CPU_NAME}")

      OUTPUT "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/qemu.cfg"

      OUTPUT "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/qemu.cfg"

      DEPENDS "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/config.inc"
      COMMENT "No CPU_CONFIG_QEMU_CONVERTER; embedding empty qemu.cfg for ${CPU_NAME}"

    WORKING_DIRECTORY "${OBJ_SC_DIR}"
    DEPENDS "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/qemu.cfg"
    COMMENT "Building qemu cfg object for ${CPU_NAME}"

1	// The phase-plan executor (F6) -- the C++ analog of runner.run_session, minus
2	// the dropped QEMU2 handback. run_plan spawns each leg of a Plan in order,
3	// threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward (leg N's --handoff-out is
4	// leg N+1's --resume-from-qemu), and reports each leg's mcycle/minstret.
5	//
6	// plan_argvs is the pure core (no spawn, no mmap): it resolves each Step's
7	// engine + role against the registry and fills the invoke template with the
8	// threaded state paths, so the argv construction is unit-testable in isolation.
9	#ifndef ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
10	#define ANDESIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
11	
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
16	#include "plan.hpp"
17	#include "process.hpp"
18	
19	namespace andes_sim {
20	
21	// The framework-owned values shared by every leg of a run: the resolved
22	// shared-mmap path/size/base and the QEMU plugin path. Per-leg values
23	// (bin/state_in/state_out) are derived by plan_argvs from this + the threading.
24	struct RuntimeCtx {
25	  std::string mmap_path;
26	  long long mem_size = 0;
27	  std::string mmap_base = "0x0";
28	  std::string plugin_path;
29	  // QEMU `-readconfig` file matching the accurate engine's ISA, distilled from
30	  // its config.inc (the engine's `--print-qemu-config`). Empty => the fast leg
31	  // keeps its descriptor's default `-cpu` (engines without the flag; FA2).
32	  std::string qemu_cfg;
33	};
34	
35	// hw-config sync: the QEMU fast leg models the hardware the accurate-leg
36	// engine measures, so its -cpu vlen follows that engine's descriptor. 512 is
37	// the fallback for engines that report none. One definition, used by both the
38	// plan executor ({vlen} fill) and the hybrid banner.
39	inline long synced_vlen(long engine_vlen) {
40	  return engine_vlen > 0 ? engine_vlen : 512;
41	}
42	
43	// A trigger's per-leg argv contribution, dispatched by the leg's role. The
44	// QEMU plugin takes its trigger as a comma-suffix folded INTO the one `-plugin`
45	// token (so it rides the `{trigger}` placeholder); vsim takes separate tokens
46	// appended to its argv. marker contributes nothing (plugin/vsim detect the markers
47	// themselves).
48	struct LegTriggerArgs {
49	  std::string plugin_suffix;        // qemu fast-leg: appended to {trigger}
50	  std::vector<std::string> extra;   // vsim accurate-leg: appended tokens
51	};
52	
53	// Map `t` onto `role`'s argv contribution. marker -> empty. pc -> qemu
54	// `,enter_pc=<enter_pc>` / vsim `--hybrid-exit-pc <exit_pc>`. Roles other
55	// than fast-leg/accurate-leg get nothing. A missing required param or an
56	// unknown trigger kind sets `err` (and returns an empty contribution).
57	//
58	// NOTE (altitude debt): these flag spellings are framework-side per-engine
59	// knowledge -- the one place F9 hardcodes a fast/accurate engine's CLI, unlike
60	// the base argv which comes from each engine's `--describe` invoke template.
61	// This is a deliberate scope cut: the principled form (per-(trigger,role) argv
62	// templates carried in `--describe`, filled by build_argv like `invoke`) would
63	// extend the F2 engine contract and is left for a later feature.
64	LegTriggerArgs leg_trigger_args(const Trigger& t, const std::string& role,
65	                                std::string& err);
66	
67	// Turn an accurate engine's `<bin> --print-qemu-config` probe into a QEMU
68	// `-readconfig` file under `workdir`. On a clean probe (exit 0, non-empty
69	// stdout) writes `workdir/qemu.cfg` and returns its path; on any failure
70	// (engine without the flag -> the parser throws -> non-zero exit; timeout;
71	// spawn failure; empty output; unwritable dir) returns "" -- the tolerant
72	// fallback that leaves the fast leg on its descriptor's default -cpu.
73	std::string stage_qemu_cfg(const std::string& workdir, const RunResult& probe);
74	
75	// Build every step's concrete argv, threading state files under `workdir`:
76	//   state_in[0]  = ""                       (cold start; no resume)
77	//   state_in[i]  = state_out[i-1]           (prior leg's drain)
78	//   state_out[i] = workdir/"state-<i>.bin"  (this leg's drain)
79	// Each step's engine is looked up in `engines` by id and its `role` template is
80	// filled via build_argv. Pure (no spawn). Returns one argv per step; on any
81	// error (unknown engine/role, unresolved placeholder) returns {} and sets `err`.
82	std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> plan_argvs(
83	    const Plan& plan, const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
84	    const std::string& workdir, const RuntimeCtx& ctx, std::string& err);
85	
86	// The exit code a leg returns after draining its state and handing off (the
87	// driver-side mirror of vsim's kExitHandoffToQemu). Every plan step is a drain
88	// step, so this is the expected per-leg exit.
89	constexpr int kDrainRc = 200;
90	
91	struct PlanOptions {
92	  int timeout_ms = 90000;     // per-leg spawn timeout
93	  int expect_rc = kDrainRc;   // drain success code
94	  std::string plugin_path;    // "" => $VSIM_PLUGIN else repo default
95	  bool dry_run = false;       // build argvs (incl. qemu_cfg) but spawn nothing

# Playbook: hybrid resume dies with `exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr=3`

Scope: a hybrid run (`./andesim run --mode hybrid`) on a freshly configured /
freshly built vsim engine aborts in the accurate leg with:

```
[critical] fatal exception: exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr=3
```

Repos referenced:
- driver / plugin / harness: `/home/nick/work/andesim`
- vsim engine + hybrid orchestration: `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim`

---

## 1. What the message means

The thrower is `exec_progbuf()` in
`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp` (line 201-205).
It writes a short instruction sequence into the RISC-V Debug Module **Program
Buffer**, tells the halted hart to execute it, then reads back
`abstractcs.cmderr`. The exception escapes to the `catch` in
`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/main.cpp:543` which prints the
`[critical] fatal exception:` line and exits 1 (so the driver then reports a
"plan step 1: expected exit 200, got 1" style error).

`cmderr` is the RISC-V Debug Spec abstract-command error code:

| cmderr | meaning |
|--------|---------|
| 1 | busy |
| 2 | not supported |
| 3 | **exception - the hart took an architectural exception while executing the injected instructions** |
| 4 | halt/resume |
| 5 | bus error |

So cmderr=3 means: one of the instructions the resume flow injected into the
Program Buffer **trapped inside the hart**. In this flow only two trap classes
occur in practice:

1. **Illegal instruction** - the instruction touches an extension or CSR the
   engine's RTL does not implement (no FPU -> `fld`/`fsd` trap; no V ->
   `vsetvl`/`vle8.v`/`vse8.v` trap; `csrrw` to an unimplemented CSR traps), or
   the extension is off in `mstatus` (FS/VS = Off, which on a core *without*
   the extension is WARL-pinned to Off, so the enable write silently no-ops).
2. **Load/store access fault** - the sweep's `ld`/`sd`/`fld`/`fsd`/
   `vle8.v`/`vse8.v` addresses the shared-mmap scratch page at a guest
   physical address the engine's memory decode does not map.

**Important discriminator built into the code:** the Andes/M-ext CSR sweep
(`csr_sweep()` in the same header) catches a faulting batch, bisects it one
CSR at a time, and rethrows a *named* error:
`csr_sweep: CSR 0x... raised cmderr -- the caps map over-claims a CSR ...`.
Therefore, if you see the **raw** `exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr=3`
message, the fault is **NOT** in the Andes/M-ext CSR list. It is one of the
fixed Program-Buffer sequences: the GPR/FPR block sweeps, the V data sweep,
the Tier-B `vsetvl`, or a single `csrrw` fallback.

---

## 2. Where it can throw, in run order

A first hybrid run on a fresh engine executes, inside the one vsim process,
in this order (`Simulator::apply_resume_from_qemu`,
`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/simulator.hpp:208`):

**Phase 0 - LG3 reset-baseline capture** (runs *before* resume; a freshly
built engine binary always misses the `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim` cache, so this
always runs on the first hybrid run of a new build):

| PB sequence | instructions | traps when |
|---|---|---|
| GPR block store | `sd x1..x30, off(x31)` | scratch page not mapped/writable |
| FPR block store (if state FLAG_FP) | `fsd f0..f31, off(x5)` | **engine has no FPU** (FS pinned Off -> illegal insn), or scratch fault |
| Andes+M-ext CSR sweep | `csrr` + `sd` per CSR | caps over-claim - but this one throws the NAMED `csr_sweep: CSR 0x...` error, not the raw one |
| V dump sweep (if FLAG_V) | `vsetvl` then `vse8.v v0..v24` | **engine has no V** (illegal insn), or scratch fault |

**Phase 1 - `ResumeDriver::resume()`**
(`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp:146`):

| step | PB sequence | traps when |
|---|---|---|
| FPR reload (FLAG_FP) | `fld f0..f31, off(x5)` | no FPU / scratch fault |
| fcsr, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, mcycle, minstret | abstract write first; on abstract cmderr, PB fallback `csrrw x0, csr, x5` | the CSR does not exist on this engine (FP/V CSRs on a no-FP/no-V core) |
| V reload (FLAG_V) | `vsetvl` + `vle8.v v0..v24` | no V / scratch fault |
| Tier-B vtype+vl | `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` | no V |
| GPR reload | `ld x1..x31, off(x31)` | scratch fault |
| Andes+M-ext restore | abstract tolerant writes only | never throws (clears cmderr per CSR) |

Note: both phases print the identical `[critical]` line, and the andesim
driver *hides* vsim's `[info]` log lines (commit b86d168), so from the driver
you cannot tell which phase died. Section 4 shows how to tell.

---

## 3. Root causes on a freshly configured engine, ranked

### RC1 (by far the most common): QEMU fast leg models MORE ISA than the new engine

## 5. Fixes

**Fix 1 - regenerate the ISA sync (empty qemu.cfg).**
In `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim`:

```sh

./build_vsim.sh          # or re-run the cmake build for the engine target
$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_<cfg> --print-qemu-config   # now non-empty
```

The rebuilt binary embeds `build/V<cfg>/obj_sc/qemu.cfg`; the driver picks it
up automatically on the next `andesim run` (no driver change needed).

**Fix 2 - make the family match an instantiable QEMU model.**
The engine name's prefix before the first `_` must be a real Andes QEMU CPU
(`qemu-system-riscv64 -cpu help | grep andes`), because both the qemu.cfg
`driver=` name and (ideally) the fast leg's `-cpu` derive from it. If your
fresh engine is not in the ax45mpv family, know that today the driver still
pins `-cpu andes-ax45mpv` for the hybrid fast leg
(`driver/engine_registry.cpp:52-53`) - the qemu.cfg globals for another
family will not apply. Options, in order of preference:
- Framework fix: derive the fast-leg `-cpu` from the accurate engine's family
  (same `REGEX REPLACE "_.*$"` rule) instead of hardcoding ax45mpv - this is
  the real root-cause repair for non-ax45mpv engines.
- Interim: reproduce the shell harness pairing manually - `tests/e2e.sh`
  takes `QEMU_CPU=andes-<family>,vlen=<VLEN>` (see
  `scripts/run_e2e.sh:123-124` for the ax66_makatau <-> andes-ax66,vlen=128
  precedent) and runs the same two-leg flow.

**Fix 3 - extension ON in the base model but absent in the engine.**
The converter never emits `off`, so pick a base QEMU model whose defaults are
a subset of the engine ISA (Fix 2 usually achieves this: the same-family
model matches by construction), or extend
`config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py::_collect_isa_props` to force-off extensions the
config lacks (`v`, `f`, `d` are the ones that bite: their state transport
executes real instructions in the Program Buffer).

**Fix 4 - memory map (RC2).**
The engine must map `[--shared-mem-base, base + mem_size + 4096)` as plain
RAM in hybrid mode. Check the fresh config's `NDS_ILM_BASE` / `NDS_DLM_BASE`
do not fall inside the window (default window: `0x0 .. 0x08001000` for the
128 MiB default), and `--print-memmap` shows the interconnect actually
decoding it. If the program needs the whole window, remember the top page is
reserved for the transport scratch - the driver already rejects ELFs that
reach into it, but a shrunken engine RAM window is the engine's problem to
fix, not the driver's.

**Fix 5 - caps map (only if the error is the NAMED csr_sweep variant, or a
poll timeout/hang).**
Bind the new config.inc macro in
`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp`
(absent macro reads as "feature off" - so a renamed macro silently drops the
gate) and/or add the CSR's gate case in `andes_gate_for()`
(`andes_caps.hpp` - an unlisted CSR defaults to ALWAYS = transported
unconditionally). Validate offline without running anything:

```sh
python3 /home/nick/work/andesim/scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py \
    /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/V<cfg>/obj_sc/config.inc
# must equal the "andes_csrs" list from `sim_<cfg> --describe`
# drift guard: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_caps_parity.sh
```

**Verify the fix.**

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --engine verilator:<cfg> --trigger marker --verify <elf>
JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh        # regression sweep on the stock engine
```

`--verify` matters here: it keeps the full drain and diffs the round-trip, so
an ISA fix that merely stops the crash but drops state (e.g. V silently off
on both sides now) is caught by the state diff, and a fresh reset-baseline is
captured for the new binary automatically (cache key includes the sim
binary's mtime/size, so no stale-baseline cleanup is needed).

## 6. Quick reference

Fault-to-cause map for the raw error:

| first faulting PB insn | likely cause |
|---|---|
| `fsd`/`fld` (FPR sweep) | state FLAG_FP set, engine has no FPU -> RC1 |
| `vsetvl`, `vle8.v`, `vse8.v` | state FLAG_V set, engine has no V -> RC1 |
| `csrrw x0, <csr>, x5` (fallback) | abstract write NAK'd then CSR truly absent (fcsr/vstart/... on no-FP/no-V core) -> RC1 |
| `ld`/`sd` (GPR sweep) | scratch page unmapped/blocked -> RC2 |

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp` | thrower; `exec_progbuf`, `pb_block_sweep`, `csr_sweep`, `pb_v_data_sweep` |
| `vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` | resume order; `write_csr_abstract_or_pb` fallback |
| `vsim_andesim/src/simulator.hpp` | `apply_resume_from_qemu`: baseline capture runs before resume |
| `vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/andes_caps{,_config}.hpp` | CSR capability gates from config.inc |
| `vsim_andesim/cmake/VerilatorHelpers.cmake` | qemu.cfg generation + family-name rule |
